hypothesis.title: Serialize the process-global override and stats state so config tests stop racing
hypothesis.description: EXTRA_OVERRIDES (static Mutex<Vec<String>> in spur-core/src/simulator/config_override.rs) and util_stats::snapshot() are process-global, but tests/config_override_effect.rs and the in-crate unit test loads_a_file_and_applies_overrides_into_a_usable_config both mutate them under cargo's parallel test threads, so one test's assignments/counters can leak into another's session. Fix: (a) add an RAII guard — e.g. `config_override::scoped_overrides(vec![...]) -> OverrideGuard` that takes a dedicated test mutex, installs, and restores on Drop — and route every test through it; (b) have session() in the integration test acquire the same guard so stats snapshots are taken while no other session is running, or move to a per-session stats handle instead of the global. Then re-run the full regression suite to confirm the failure that closed the parent was harness contamination, not the override path.
hypothesis.rationale: The parent closed on `regression suite failed` while every mechanism claim it made actually held. If the failure is cross-test contamination from two process-global statics, every future config/sweep test that touches overrides inherits the same flake, and each one costs a full regression cycle to diagnose. Fixing the isolation once unblocks the whole sweep-tooling line and lets the parent's already-working code be re-judged on its merits.
hypothesis.generalityArgument: Touches only Rust test scaffolding and a global-state accessor in the config layer; no protocol, scheduler, or VR semantics are involved, and it asserts nothing about any spec.
hypothesis.notes: Falsified if the regression suite still fails with all override/stats state serialized — that would point at a real defect elsewhere in the override path.
